---
title: "ifelse() fails on a NULL branch, but only when it is used"
ref: FLW-02
categories: [Control flow]
impact: cryptique
extrait: 'ifelse(FALSE, 1, NULL)'
attendu: "`NULL` or `NA` for the missing value"
versions: "All"
source: "Slack ThinkR (2021)"
---

::: {.piege}
```{r}
params <- list(threshold = 10)
ifelse(TRUE, yes = params$threshold, no = params$default)
ifelse(c(TRUE, FALSE), yes = params$threshold, no = params$default)
```
:::

## Why

`params$default` does not exist, so `$` quietly returns `NULL`. As long as the test holds only `TRUE` values, `ifelse()` never needs the `no` branch and does not even evaluate it, hence the 10 with no error.

As soon as a `FALSE` shows up, `ifelse()` recycles `no` to the length of the test with `rep()`, which returns `NULL` (the first warning), then tries to assign it into the result: "replacement has length zero". The message talks about replacement and zero length without ever naming the faulty variable, and the bug only appears with some data.

## The remedy

Check the value before using it, and give it an explicit fallback.

::: {.piege}
```{r}
default <- params$default
if (is.null(default)) {
  default <- NA
}
ifelse(c(TRUE, FALSE), yes = params$threshold, no = default)
```
:::
